instructions: Rinse the rice in a medium pot with cold water, swirling and draining until the water runs almost clear. Add 1 3/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered until you serve.
Cut each zucchini in half lengthwise, then slice across into half-moons about 1/4 inch thick. Mince the garlic and thinly slice the 3 green onions.
Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the zucchini in one layer with 1/2 tsp of the salt and half the garlic. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add 2 tbsp water and cook for 2 minutes, until the slices turn translucent and are just tender. Don't let them go mushy. Transfer them into a bowl.
Repeat with the remaining 1 tbsp oil, zucchini, 1/2 tsp salt and garlic.
Return all the zucchini to the skillet. Add the green onions, sesame oil and sesame seeds and stir for 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Lead is Korean Bapsang's hobak bokkeum (4.84 from 25): quarter-inch zucchini stir-fried with garlic and a seasoning, a splash of water, then green onion, sesame oil and sesame seeds at the end. The source seasons with saeujeot (salted shrimp) and lists plain salt as the swap, so this uses salt and stays vegan. Scaled from 1 zucchini for 2 to 3 for 4, cooked in two batches so the pan stays hot. The list sells it as a light meal with rice, so rice is included; the sources don't add a protein and neither does this.
